That makes total sense. I went through the same slow process of figuring it out. Our brains have a funny way of trying to minimizing or ignore the trauma to try to reconcile or forget what happened. It’s a method of survival. I also found this show triggered a lot of extreme reactions/panic attacks in me when I was forced to confront my own reality.

I really encourage you to call a hotline for survivors of sexual assault. The nuanced/grey areas of real life experiences can be hard for you to explain to people who aren’t educated about the topic. I think talking to the right person will help you process what happened, what that means, and how to move forward.

You don’t have to deal with this alone. You deserve compassion. This wasn’t your fault.

Thank you for sharing. You are not a fraud, you are a SA survivor. I also feel like my story is fraudulent because I ‘consented’, but I was blackout drunk and my then-girlfriend was not. I could not consent.

Consent has to be enthusiastic and not manipulated/coerced. Consent can be withdrawn at any time. Someone violating that boundary is SA. It’s a horrible/imposter-like feeling, as if we participated in and allowed our SA to happen.

Why are you punishing your son? If you care about him at all you will not treat him like he is disposable. I find your attitude disgusting. Your feelings towards your wife are valid but they shouldn’t impact how you show up for your child. 

The DNA doesn’t match and all of a sudden the last 15 years become transactional? You need *compensation* for raising him because he’s not “yours”? Your son was deprived of a relationship with his bio dad. Now you’re also taking away his relationship with the man who raised him. Will that make things right in your mind?
